post_title: What total revenue will Nebius Group report for Q3 2026?

question.title: What total revenue will Nebius Group report for Q3 2026?
question.description:
Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ: NBIS) is an Amsterdam-headquartered AI infrastructure ("neocloud") company, spun out of Yandex in 2024, whose main business is selling GPU compute through its Nebius AI cloud; it also holds stakes or interests in Toloka, Avride, TripleTen and ClickHouse. The company will release its third-quarter 2026 financial results on Thursday, November 12, 2026, before the US market open, with a conference call at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time the same day (https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-group-announces-date-of-third-quarter-2026-results-and-conference-call). Because results land pre-market, forecasters have only a short window before the number is public.

Recent trajectory (total group revenue): Q3 2025 $146.1M, Q4 2025 $227.7M, Q1 2026 $399.0M, Q2 2026 $582.3M (+454% year over year). First-half 2026 revenue was $981.3M. In Q2 2026, Nebius AI cloud revenue was $574.9M (+514% YoY), group adjusted EBITDA was $236.2M (AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin around 50%), and annualized run-rate revenue (ARR) reached $3.0B at end-June 2026, up 598% YoY and 56% quarter over quarter.

Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0–3.4B on August 12, 2026. With $981.3M booked in H1, that guidance implies roughly $2.02–2.42B of revenue in H2 2026, i.e. a steep second-half ramp. Sell-side consensus for Q3 2026 sits around $905–940M: Equibles cites a $904.8M consensus (analyst range $876.6M–$942.6M) and forecasts $934.5M itself (https://equibles.com/research/nebius-group-nbis-q3-2026-earnings-preview-and-forecast), while Zacks showed a $916.8M consensus from six estimates (range $884.8M–$942.6M) in late October 2026. Q4 2026 consensus is roughly $1.45–1.53B; summed, consensus full-year revenue (~$3.38B) sits near the top of the guidance range, so a slower capacity ramp is a live downside scenario while faster capacity activation is a live upside one. Historically the revenue surprise has been small and two-sided: Q1 2026 beat consensus by 6.6% and Q2 2026 by about 1%, while Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 missed by roughly 5%.

Operational context: Nebius is racing to bring data-centre capacity online (Finland; a 240 MW site near Lille in France whose first 60 MW phase is due to open in December 2026; US sites) and has arranged a $3.5B Citi financing facility against a large contracted backlog. In late October 2026 the stock and the wider neocloud sector sold off on credit/financing concerns, Microsoft's lighter-than-expected capex and warnings about neocloud debt; NBIS traded roughly $154–$182 between October 26 and 29, 2026 and is well below its 2026 highs. Any delay in energizing capacity or in customer deployments would show up directly in quarterly revenue.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves based on Nebius Group N.V.'s (NASDAQ: NBIS) reported total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as published in the company's Q3 2026 earnings release, scheduled for release before market open on November 12, 2026 and posted at https://nebius.com/investor-hub. The resolving value is the total revenue line (labelled "Revenues" in Nebius's recent results tables) for the three months ended September 30, 2026 in the consolidated results of that release, expressed in millions of US dollars (a figure published as "934.5" in a table headed "In USD $ millions", or as $934,500 thousand, resolves as 934.5; if the release reports in thousands, divide by 1,000). The value as first published governs, even if later revised or restated. If the release has not been published by the expected resolution date, resolution waits and resolves to that figure once it is published; if Nebius Group never publishes a total revenue figure for the three months ended September 30, 2026, the question is annulled.
